> `obs_count` is **not comparable across runs** — most fetchers report rows merged this run, thirteen fall back to the whole store when nothing was written. To ask how big this source is, count the store. See ledger R326 and the comment in `updater/state.py`.

> A `partial` NEVER sets `last_success_utc` (R231). A source reading `last SUCCESS: NEVER` may be ingesting millions of rows perfectly well and failing one sub-unit. Check `obs_count` and the run history before concluding it is dead.

> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> Two scripts: the primary CBS/LBS path (ingest_bis_cbs_lbs.py) downloads whole-table flat-CSV zips with NO date filter, so gate on HEAD Last-Modified/Content-Length and re-download+rebuild only when the zip changes; the secondary SDMX path (ingest_bis_full.py) could do sdmx_delta via startPeriod but degrades to per-flow re-pull and both scripts write to the same dir - bulk_snapshot is the binding strategy for the source.

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: HTTP HEAD Last-Modified / Content-Length on the two bulk zip URLs (data.bis.org CBS.zip & LBS.zip) - the zips ARE dated upstream but the code reads no date today. Replace the >10000-byte download skip and the out_path-exists ingest no-op with a HEAD-gated re-download. (SDMX path ingest_bis_full.py: optional startPeriod=<last_year> on /data/{flow}, but BIS exposes no clean per-flow vintage so it degrades to full re-pull.)
- `since_param`: n/a for bulk CBS/LBS (no date param); SDMX path would use startPeriod=<last_obs_year> on /data/{flow}
- `out_paths_note`: Multi-file AND multi-script collision: ingest_bis_cbs_lbs.py writes data/clean_full/bis/CBS.parquet (37.5MB) & LBS.parquet (183MB) with raw zips cached in data/raw/bis_bulk; ingest_bis_full.py writes WS_*.parquet (giants chunked as <DID>__<FREQ>[__<VAL>].parquet) into the SAME data/clean_full/bis dir plus _manifest.json/_catalog.json. Force-refresh must clear BOTH the cached zips (>10000B skip) and the parquets (out-exists no-op); deleting only the parquet rebuilds from the STALE cached zip.
- `rate_note`: No API key. Polite custom UA. License bis-attrib-nc (non-commercial, attribution). Bulk: 600s timeout, resumable HTTP Range (LBS zip ~356MB). SDMX: per-socket 120s timeout, 5x retry, CHUNK_WORKERS=6 (BIS throttles per-connection bandwidth on big extracts).

**Fetcher module**: [`updater/strategies/fetchers/bis.py`](../../updater/strategies/fetchers/bis.py)

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
S1 bulk fetcher — BIS Consolidated & Locational Banking Statistics (data.bis.org, no key).

BIS publishes two flat-CSV bulk zips at STABLE urls (no date or version in the path):
    CBS  https://data.bis.org/static/bulk/WS_CBS_PUB_csv_flat.zip
    LBS  https://data.bis.org/static/bulk/WS_LBS_D_PUB_csv_flat.zip
so the honest change signal is each object's own HTTP validator (ETag / Last-Modified /
Content-Length) — re-download only when it moves.

WHY THE INGEST COULD NOT SIMPLY BE WRAPPED. jobs/ingest_bis_cbs_lbs.py is backfill-shaped:
`download()` returns early when the zip is already on disk and `ingest_zip()` returns early
when the parquet already exists. Both are right for a one-off load and inert as an updater —
scheduled, they would do nothing forever while reporting success. The parse was also inline in
`ingest_zip`, writing straight to a ParquetWriter, so there was nothing callable to reuse.

Rather than copy the parser (which breaks the duplication invariant the moment either side is
edited), the parse was EXTRACTED into `ingest_bis_cbs_lbs.iter_rows()` — a pure generator
yielding (series_key, obs_date, value, freq) with no skip rules, no writer and no logging
policy. The ingest now delegates to it too, so there is exactly ONE parse and the fetcher and
the first-pass ingest cannot drift apart.

MEMORY. The CBS/LBS flat CSVs are tens of millions of rows, so rows are accumulated in
BATCH-sized chunks and merged incrementally rather than materialised whole.

HONEST-STATUS: a HEAD/validator failure -> the zip is treated as changed (fetch anyway, which
merge dedups) rather than silently skipped. A download or parse failure -> transient_unit for
that zip only, so CBS failing cannot stop LBS publishing. A zip that parses to ZERO rows ->
structural_unit and its vintage is NOT advanced, so a parser break resurfaces next run instead
of being sealed in.
```

</details>

**Ingest script(s)**: `jobs/ingest_bis_cbs_lbs.py`, `jobs/ingest_bis_full.py`

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='bis'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source bis --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source bis --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('bis');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source bis
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
